kiln_p17_001.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_001.text: Summer announced itself through the water boy's empty yoke. He came through the gate on time and set the two buckets down as though they contained a delicate excuse. The delivery channel had stopped running at the pottery branch. Upstream workers said the town was clearing silt, and nobody knew whether water would return before noon. Luo looked at the clay already opened on the benches. Zhu looked at the wash basin. Peng looked at the kettle. Three ordinary uses suddenly occupied the same small silence. Yue offered to fetch drinking water and was told to take the light containers.

kiln_p17_002.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_002.text: The public well was crowded, but not lawless. The keeper had separate places for households, animals and trades, and the posted draw periods were being adjusted to the flow. A baker complained that pottery used water to make ugly jars. A potter answered that bread used water to become expensive crumbs. The keeper told both men to save their breath for hauling. Yue grinned despite herself and waited in the household line for the hall's drinking supply. Her personal rank did not shorten the queue. The woman ahead asked her to hold a sleeping child's cloth out of the mud.

kiln_p17_003.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_003.text: By noon the channel remained dry. Tan returned from the town maintenance desk with the notice: the silt work had exposed a damaged small gate, requiring repair before the branch reopened. The hall's purchased delivery was delayed, not secretly withdrawn to favor a rival. The carrier could provide a limited ordinary tank from an approved source at an added journey cost. The owner approved enough for essential washing, drinking support and the clay that could not safely wait. New nonessential mixing would pause. Luo covered the opened body and went to tell the workers before anyone invented a better supply.

kiln_p17_004.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_004.text: 'Can we use yesterday's settling water?' Jian asked from the cold table. Zhu pointed to the labeled container. Its suspended glaze and cleaning residue made it unsuitable for drinking, skin washing or the qualified clay mixture. Some could serve a defined rough floor-cleaning task, with the resulting residue collected. Reusing water was not the same as calling every wet thing clean. Jian made a face. 'I was hoping for an ingenious answer.' 'That was one,' she said. 'It saves the floor water without poisoning your tea.' Yue laughed into her cup and nearly proved the importance of a dry rag.

kiln_p17_005.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_005.text: The tank arrived behind a patient donkey which seemed to regard every pottery crisis as an excuse for inferior carrots. Tan checked the source slip and quantity with the carrier before receiving it. The owner paid the added approved journey cost. Workers filled the drinking and wash containers first, then the covered clay supply under Luo's schedule. There was no new water for a speculative festival batch. The donkey ate a carrot Zhu had actually bought, not one stolen from the kitchen ration. Jian declared it the only person rewarded for lateness. The carrier said it had arrived when paid.

kiln_p17_006.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_006.text: Yue helped cover the interrupted drying shelves with breathable cloth rather than seal them damp. Warm wind was drawing moisture from the rims faster than the thick feet could follow. Zhu turned one sample toward the light and showed the first shallow distortion. 'It wants to become a hat,' Jian said. 'Then we must charge it for a head,' Zhu answered. They moved the current pieces into the qualified slower space and kept a comparison of the changed conditions. The joke made the work lighter; it did not make the crooked sample saleable. Yue liked the difference.

kiln_p17_007.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_007.text: The failed rim sent them back beneath the stairs. Peng retrieved a summer entry whose triumphant heading promised quicker drying at lower cost. Its retained pieces told a less cheerful story: several cracked feet and one corrected schedule written on the reverse. The main success concerned thicker storage jars, not the present shallow bowls. Zhu unfolded the original note and swore at the copied summary. Jian offered to amend his index. Peng handed him the correction form and a paid hour. Yue watched the dry old paper acquire present value through the very failure its first author had almost hidden.

kiln_p17_008.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_008.text: The owner had hoped to enter the town's midsummer household-ware exhibition. A prize could attract fair ordinary orders after a winter full of public notices. Now the water delay and drying correction threatened the decorative bowls. She asked Zhu what could actually be finished. The trimmer named a small number with a longer schedule and no promise of a prize. The owner sat down. 'I wanted the hall to look clever again.' Zhu said it would look foolish if the feet split on a judge's table. They agreed to show fewer sound pieces and one honest failed sample.

kiln_p17_009.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_009.text: Peng wanted the failed sample to carry its full note, not a witty label about brave experiments. Tan worried customers would remember the crack and forget the qualification of the sound bowls. Yue suggested a separate cold display where visitors could compare the bodies, uses and drying conditions. The exhibition organizer allowed a small teaching table but required an ordinary attendant and safe handling. Yue's earlier sample role fitted the task. She accepted the paid hours, while Luo remained responsible for the technical explanation. No charged demonstration would be added merely to draw a larger crowd.

kiln_p17_010.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_010.text: At the channel repair, the town's gate worker showed Luo the broken support and the proposed ordinary replacement. The pottery foreman had no authority to operate it, but could explain the branch demand and timing. Yue accompanied him to carry the light copies. Water stood upstream of the gate, dull green beneath willow shade. A merchant claimed that a cultivator should push the stream through another path. Yue asked where that path would discharge and which banks could withstand it. The merchant lost interest before those practical questions ended. The gate worker gave her an appreciative, exhausted smile.

kiln_p17_011.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_011.text: The repair needed timber from the common maintenance yard and two recovered workers to fit it. One was caring for a child that morning; the posted schedule had already included his later shift. Tan arranged the hall's voluntary paid contribution to hauling approved material, with no claim to control the town gate afterward. Yue worked only at the permitted waist-height carry. She felt ordinary usefulness return through muscles that no longer startled her with pain. The town worker offered her a heavier end. She declined and took the lighter piece without explaining her whole winter to everyone nearby.

kiln_p17_012.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_012.text: Jian could join the supervised cold hauling task but not improvise at the gate mechanism. He asked the maintenance worker to explain the failure while they rested. The answer involved softened timber around an old fastener, not a mysterious theft of water. The boy ran a finger over the worn piece after permission. 'I would have blamed the upstream shops,' he admitted. The worker said he had heard that rumor twice before breakfast. Yue watched Jian place the actual explanation into his notebook. It felt like a modest antidote to a habit of making institutions into single hostile persons.

kiln_p17_013.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_013.text: The branch reopened after the approved repair and ordinary leak check. The hall received its scheduled water later that day, with the temporary tank balance measured before settling the delivery account. The owner did not try to keep both supplies unrecorded because shortages might return. The extra reserve had a finite volume and defined use. Tan marked it for the following week's essential and current-process needs. Yue was glad when the practical talk ended and someone finally offered the workers lunch. A functioning gate was important. So was eating before the afternoon tasks turned hunger into another clever mistake.

kiln_p17_014.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_014.text: Luo's first posterior lesson took place two mornings later after Yue's recovered quiet week and a fresh movement check. The comparison room was cool enough that the stone bench felt almost wet through cloth. He laid out the agreed lower input, guarded receiver and separate interruption before she stood. This was the distinct posterior heel and calf path toward the hip, with its outward return; it wasn't the anterior route renamed backward. Yue traced the difference with no personal input first. The unfamiliar map made her clumsy. Luo asked her to slow down until eagerness stopped choosing her feet.

kiln_p17_015.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_015.text: She could identify the anterior pair by its established inward and outward return. The posterior preparation had a different contact pattern and release sequence. Luo had her alternate the empty traces with rest, naming each without forcing a full circuit between them. When she confused the outward heel point, he stopped the dry exercise and changed the stance marker. 'A new name isn't a new route,' he said. 'Nor is an old route wearing a new name.' Yue repeated the separation until she could explain it without glancing at the slate. No leg input had yet been admitted.

kiln_p17_016.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_016.text: The first posterior admission was an eighth input unit spread across four ordinary breaths, no more than a thirty-second in one breath. The receiver was not asked to lift the useful quarter weight. Luo watched the measured contact and kept the grounded release ready; Yue could interrupt independently. The new inward path gathered unevenly near the calf on the third breath. She stopped rather than add the remaining fraction to make the page look complete. The released input went to the rated ground. Her hand shook with disappointment, though the task had done exactly what a cautious first task needed.

kiln_p17_017.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_017.text: Luo wrote the actual partial admission and interruption, not a successful eighth because that had been the planned amount. Yue sat until her ordinary movement felt normal. The calf tension subsided without treatment beyond rest, and the clinician found no new loss of touch or movement on the requested check. There would be no further posterior input that day. 'I have become very good at disappointing a slate,' she said. Luo looked at the incomplete row. 'This one seems satisfied.' She laughed at the foreman's solemn answer and found the disappointment less hungry for a secret second attempt.

kiln_p17_018.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_018.text: On the next morning her ordinary touch, grip and leg movement remained normal. The lower task resumed on a separate recovered day with a revised stance and the same eighth-over-four maximum. This time the short inward and outward return completed cleanly into the guarded receiver and released fully. It established a first bounded posterior passage, not useful load mastery. Yue could distinguish its posterior heel-calf-hip contact from the anterior foot-knee-hip path when Luo changed the dry naming order afterward. She left the room with two leg maps in her notes and the old fourth-stage record still true.

kiln_p17_019.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_019.text: Jian asked how many pairs she now possessed. Yue said the method would count the full four-pair stage only after the agreed reserve, purity, useful tasks, three recovered assessments and following-day checks. She had begun the fourth route; that was worth celebrating without renaming it completed mastery. He offered a solemn toast with water. Zhu raised her cup too and said, 'To beginnings that don't apply for senior wages.' Yue threw a cloth at her and missed. Her shoulder tolerated the low motion, but the cloth fell embarrassingly short. The room laughed until Peng ordered everyone to dry the table.

kiln_p17_020.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_020.text: Han heard about the toast and asked whether he could attend the next unqualified celebration. His latest care review permitted more warm-room inspection away from the active grit post, with a gradual schedule. He brought a lopsided uncharged cup to the supper table and said it was an ideal vessel for progress. Jian smiled, then looked away when he realized he had smiled at Han. The worker accepted the water without comment. They could share a table without naming the friendship. Yue stopped monitoring their faces and asked Zhu why the cup's handle leaned like a tired ear.

kiln_p17_021.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_021.text: The exhibition bowls required a new ordinary schedule after the weather changed again. The first comparison had prevented the worst uneven drying, but a damp night slowed the thicker foot. Zhu refused to compensate with a hotter hurried start. The owner approved fewer pieces and a longer dry hold within the paid work plan. Tan amended the exhibition count before the organizer printed it. Yue watched the hall give up the pleasant shape of a promise while keeping the promise's purpose. The sound bowls would reach the table. The imaginary large display could remain imaginary without anyone hiding a crack.

kiln_p17_022.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_022.text: Peng found an old letter asking the workshop to send a prize bowl to the capital. Its author had made a beautiful glaze with an unstable foot and asked the recipient to overlook it for art. The retained reply refused the fragile gift for daily use and admired the color separately. Zhu read the exchange aloud with exaggerated dignity. 'At last, someone who knows a bowl has to stand up.' Yue asked if the color could be studied for decorative tiles. Peng said yes, after identifying the mixture and firing record rather than copying the letter's praise as a recipe.

kiln_p17_023.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_023.text: That suggestion gave Zhu a new want which had nothing to do with repaired credit. She wanted to make a blue so deep that a plain wall seemed to hold evening. Her brace made some mixing motions awkward; Jian could perform the approved stirring while she measured and observed. They agreed the paid task and recorded her authorship of the comparison design. Yue watched the first small tile turn out a gray. Zhu held it under three different lights, then said she had successfully invented wet ash. They retained it with the mixture note and tried the next bounded comparison.

kiln_p17_024.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_024.text: The second tile bloomed unevenly where the glaze pooled. Zhu liked the color and disliked the result. A visiting decorator offered to buy it immediately as a novelty. She refused to call the effect repeatable before it had a method. The owner allowed a separate art sample sale if accurately described, with Zhu's agreed share and no claim about household durability. Zhu considered the offer overnight. She wanted income and recognition, but also wanted the next trial to remain hers to direct. Yue understood the pause. A fortunate object could create a contract before a worker understood its future.

kiln_p17_025.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_025.text: The water delay left Luo irritable for reasons he initially refused to name. He had planned the summer rota carefully, including a week away from the hall to visit his daughter's household. Every new remake and shifted drying hold seemed to eat that week. Yue asked why another qualified operator could not cover the ordinary schedule. He said of course one could, then listed seven reasons the handover would be difficult. Peng listened from the doorway. 'Those are seven items for a handover,' she said. 'Not seven reasons to keep your grandchildren waiting forever.' The foreman scowled at her accuracy.

kiln_p17_026.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_026.text: He brought the actual cover plan to the next meeting. The visiting operator would receive the current fixture qualification, weather limits, warning positions and accepted firing schedule. Tan would not add an urgent customer load during the absence without the technical approval. Yue helped prepare the comparison copies, discovering how much ordinary knowledge the foreman carried in unwritten gestures. A chalk arrow on a slate meant something different when wind came from the west. Luo finally wrote the condition beside it. 'Now someone else can be annoyed correctly,' Zhu said. He told her to make a note of that too.

kiln_p17_027.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_027.text: The covering operator arrived early enough to observe two firings before taking the role. She corrected one handover line because the safe observation post had changed after the warning-screen review. Luo accepted the correction, then looked annoyed that he had accepted it so easily. Yue watched the two experienced workers compare positions rather than trade declarations of trust. Yue felt less frightened as the handover progressed. On the morning he left, Jian carried his travel bundle to the gate under a permitted cold duty and received a stern reminder not to improve any fixtures while he was gone.

kiln_p17_028.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_028.text: Jian answered, 'Not even your hat?' Luo touched the battered brim and said the hat was independently certified to irritate his daughter. Zhu laughed so hard she dropped a clean cloth. The foreman waved from the road without looking back, which made Yue sad. He had been present through her painful shoulder months and every cautious new route. The covering operator handled the kiln, but didn't take over his cultivation teaching. Yue's posterior input sessions would pause during his short absence unless Su Yan's qualified visit and the agreed recovered conditions aligned. The next morning's ordinary work began on time.

kiln_p17_029.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_029.text: Peng used the pause to have Yue explain her posterior record in plain language. The distinction between the anterior and posterior pairs had to remain intelligible without the teacher's presence. Yue drew the contacts, named the input actually admitted and described the stopped first attempt. She separated planned eighth input from the smaller completed amount on that day. Peng asked what useful work had been established. 'A short clean passage,' Yue answered. 'Not the quarter-unit task.' The clerk nodded and handed back the page. 'Then don't let a beautiful diagram start carrying a weight your body has not.'

kiln_p17_030.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_030.text: Yue's ordinary personal practice continued at the established arm and anterior limits on the permitted recovered schedule. She worked more slowly on gathering compatible charge and releasing what the method could not safely keep. The approved finite source allowance did not increase because she wanted the four-pair threshold before summer ended. Some admitted input was lost through grounded refinement and sampling. She recorded usable reserve after that cost. One week's apparent improvement vanished when poor sleep reduced the recovered reading. Zhu found her glaring at the page and offered the gray tile as a portrait of statistical disappointment.

kiln_p17_031.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_031.text: 'It is a remarkably accurate likeness,' Yue said. She placed the tile beside the practice record until Peng asked whether it belonged to the official sample series. Yue returned it and kept the joke in her private notes instead. The act of separating those records cheered her. She could be discouraged without making the method unfair, and pleased without making a result bigger. Later that day she walked to the well with light containers and heard the baker and potter still arguing about crumbs and ugly jars. They shouted through the steam, and she bought a broken bun.

kiln_p17_032.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_032.text: The baker recognized her from the water queue and offered a broken bun that could not be sold whole. She paid the stated price rather than accept a mysterious reward for cultivation. He asked if the kiln could make a tray that kept bread warm without scorching it. Yue brought the question to Zhu instead of inventing a personal-charge answer. They examined his tray and the oven conditions. A thicker body might help distribute heat but require a changed firing and handling trial. The baker agreed to a prototype and no promise that a bowl maker understood his entire oven.

kiln_p17_033.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_033.text: That prototype gave Jian a supervised cold layout exercise with a customer use. He copied the oven dimensions twice and noticed they disagreed with the baker's remembered measurement. The supervisor asked him to check the source rather than choose the number that made the tray fit the shelf. He returned with the baker and measured the cold opening. The baker grumbled about interruptions until the resulting drawing showed why the larger guessed tray would jam. Jian wrote the correction without embarrassment turning into concealment. Yue admired the work because the answer had required asking a person, not solving a line.

kiln_p17_034.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_034.text: Zhu proposed two ordinary bodies and made small retained samples before the full tray. One resisted the heating cycle but warped enough to rock. The other remained flatter and needed a slightly slower dry schedule. The baker's first reaction was that she should simply choose the second. She agreed only after the intended ordinary heating and cleaning comparisons, because flatness alone didn't establish useful durability. He sighed. 'Your profession makes bread seem impatient.' She replied that bread had the good manners to be eaten before most long-term defects appeared. Yue nearly choked on the comparison and earned another clean-rag duty.

kiln_p17_035.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_035.text: The successful prototype was loaned for the agreed short guarded oven trial, not given away as though the result were already final. The baker supplied the heat pattern and returned it for inspection after the stated uses. A handle location needed changing for his cloth grip. The trimmer had designed the handle from her own bench habits, not his oven door. She altered the cold model and retained the earlier version. Yue watched two competent people discover that competence in one place could become inconvenience in another. The final customer order waited until both had a result they could use.

kiln_p17_036.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_036.text: Meanwhile the gray-blue tile attracted the covering operator, who wanted a small wall plaque for her household. Zhu said the odd pooled color was an accurately described art sample, not a repeatable glaze promise. The operator liked that exact object. The agreed sale gave Zhu her stated share and left the recipe and future comparisons under the maker's agreed rights. Tan wrote the terms in a short ordinary receipt. No one needed a grand contract for one small plaque. They did need to avoid selling the next year's work through a casual compliment about the first fortunate tile.

kiln_p17_037.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_037.text: Zhu carried her share to the market and bought better cloth for her hand brace. Yue expected a triumphant luxury and instead saw the trimmer comparing seams inside plain sleeves. 'Art funds comfort,' Zhu said. 'The great traditions are intact.' The seller let her try a loose fit while supporting the injured hand. She chose a cloth that would not catch on a mixing paddle and paid the actual price. On the way home she bought Yue a cheap fruit with no ceremony. The sweetness arrived as a friend's small choice, not as compensation for any official task.

kiln_p17_038.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_038.text: Peng spent the same afternoon with a former learner's incomplete record. The woman had completed several cold exercises but lost the slips when her room flooded. A teacher could remember general attendance, not each assessed task. Peng offered a funded new assessment of the safe exercises, with historical attendance noted separately. The woman was furious that she might need to prove old work again. Peng agreed the loss was unfair. She could not manufacture the missing observations. Yue heard the conversation and understood why honest limits often sounded colder than generous lies, especially to a person tired of proving herself.

kiln_p17_039.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_039.text: The former learner accepted one assessment after negotiating a time that didn't steal her wages. The owner funded the agreed session and the transport, within the independent review's provision. She passed the first cold task and stopped the second when the changed model condition exceeded the stated scope. Zhu called that an excellent stop. The woman asked whether someone would finally write it down before she left. Peng handed her the checked copy that afternoon. Yue watched her tuck it inside a cloth pouch. The woman checked her name twice before leaving.

kiln_p17_040.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_040.text: Jian asked why the former learner's stopped task counted as a success while his cold exercise still needed further repetition. Luo was away, so the appointed teacher answered from the stated rubrics. Different tasks assessed different capacities, and the remedial course required reliable stops under several changed conditions. The woman had passed the task she was assigned, not every possible operation in the hall. Jian considered the answer, then amended his comparison note. Yue was relieved to hear an question without accusation. Suspicion had once arrived before evidence. Now the boy sometimes left space for a difference to be explained.

kiln_p17_041.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_041.text: During a warm evening storm, rain reached the yard faster than the channel could carry runoff away. Workers moved drying pieces from the lowest shelf before water rose against its foot. The covering operator kept the active kiln area clear and followed the qualified weather schedule. Yue carried light cloth and read the room list from the dry boundary. Jian asked the supervisor before moving a labeled sample group, preserving its order instead of saving the jars into one anonymous pile. They lost a few unsaleable wet pieces. Yue dried the cloth, then went upstairs to change her soaked shoes.

kiln_p17_042.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_042.text: Afterward Peng found the archive still dry beneath its stairs. A drain near the entrance needed clearing; the records hadn't been protected by supernatural certainty. Yue helped inspect the threshold and lifted the approved low boxes while another worker moved the heavier shelf. The storm left the town smelling of leaf mold and wet ash. Zhu said summer had now used both too little and too much water, an unfair variety of instruction. Jian suggested invoicing the sky. Tan said its receiving clerk had an excellent reputation for never signing. Even the stern covering operator laughed.

kiln_p17_043.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_043.text: The morning after the storm, Yue found her sleep had been broken by listening for bells that hadn't rung. She deferred the personal-input task and walked through the post-storm inspection instead. The old shoulder felt normal in its permitted range, but alertness alone didn't establish a recovered training day. Han joined the cold checks under his clearance and admitted he had listened too. The sound of weather had reminded them of different hazards. Neither needed the other to pretend the reminder was foolish. They counted the damage, drank warm tea and let the next quiet night do its own work.

kiln_p17_044.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_044.text: Su Yan arrived on the planned circuit visit two days later, after the storm cleanup had ended. She brought her own teaching apparatus and would take it away again; Yue's habitual pack acquired no extra tools by association. Luo's transmitted notes and the recovered movement check gave the actual posterior starting point. Su Yan asked Yue to trace anterior and posterior contacts in changed order without input. She caught the same heel confusion once and made Yue correct the stance slowly. 'Your legs are allowed to look boring,' she said. 'They needn't perform your ambition for the room.'

kiln_p17_045.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_045.text: The next lower posterior passage used the eighth input over four ordinary breaths, completed cleanly with independent interruption and full grounded release. Su Yan waited through actual rest before a second dry comparison and declined further charged repetition that day. Yue wanted to ask for the larger step and instead asked what result would justify it. The teacher named repeated recovered lower passages, normal next-day checks and no confusion under changed naming order. She would review those records before approving a quarter input. The method moved through evidence rather than the teacher's affection, which Yue found both reassuring and inconvenient.

kiln_p17_046.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_046.text: The following morning remained normal in touch, grip and leg movement. Su Yan observed the check and wrote the lower passage's scope before leaving for another patient on the circuit. Luo would resume teaching from that actual recovered result on his return, with the agreed finite source allowance. She didn't leave Yue a secret advanced exercise to enjoy alone. At the gate Yue asked whether the final four-pair assessment could occur before the summer ended. Su Yan said it could if the person and method actually reached readiness. 'The season isn't your enemy,' she added. 'Don't appoint it your examiner.'

kiln_p17_047.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_047.text: Luo returned carrying a carved wooden animal a grandchild had insisted he keep. He tried to hide it in his travel bag, but Zhu found the head protruding beside a clean shirt. It appeared to be either a horse or a badly informed duck. The foreman said it was unquestionably a tiger. Jian offered to put it in the archive of ambitious designs. Luo threatened him with an extra copying hour, then clarified that no such paid task had been assigned. Yue laughed until the wooden tiger fell over on the table. The foreman stood it up with extraordinary tenderness.

kiln_p17_048.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_048.text: He read the covering operator's actual notes and thanked her for the corrected observation-post line. The handover had worked without making him unnecessary. He seemed to struggle with those two facts for a while, then scheduled his next family visit before the summer rota filled. Yue was glad to see a teacher choose a future outside her progress. His body and time were not limitless teaching fuel. That evening he reviewed Su Yan's posterior result with the same care he gave a firing slate. The lower passage could continue. The useful-load steps would come through the next month's recovered practice.

kiln_p17_049.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_049.text: The baker returned the prototype tray with a stained corner and an enthusiastic demand for six. Zhu inspected the stain, cleaning result and ordinary heating comparison before agreeing to the now-qualified changed handle. Tan offered a delivery date that matched the current body preparation and kiln space. The baker negotiated the price until the owner threatened to charge him for every crumb he shed on the desk. He laughed and accepted the fair written order. Jian copied the actual cold layout used in qualification, including the corrected oven measurement. The archive gained a success whose inconvenient preliminary pages remained attached.

kiln_p17_050.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_050.text: Yue visited the bakery when the first completed tray arrived. The baker used the cloth grip and showed her how the changed handle cleared his door. He offered another broken bun and she bought it at the agreed price. The bread tasted better hot, though no personal charge had entered the clay or oven. She thought of methods she'd once imagined earning. There was pleasure in a smaller competence that gave another person the awkward object their work required. When she returned, Zhu asked for the verdict. Yue handed her the paid bun and said it stood up well.

kiln_p17_051.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_051.text: Han's sister visited with a basket of summer herbs for the kitchen, not a medical remedy for either injury. She wanted her brother to stop describing the clinic pots as though they were his personal responsibility. He said he had merely been checking delivery. She raised an eyebrow so familiar that Yue understood the whole family conversation without another word. Jian entered with an approved sample list, saw the visitor and hesitated. Han took the list and introduced him by name. The sister knew the account. Her civil greeting didn't require anyone to invent a healed friendship on the spot.

kiln_p17_052.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_052.text: Later Jian said the introduction had felt more difficult than a formal reprimand. Yue asked why. 'Because he could have left me outside the sentence,' he answered. She did not tell him what Han intended. It was Han's choice, made in an ordinary work moment. The boy folded his sample copy and went back to the permitted table. Yue watched him leave without rushing after a reassurance. Friendship sometimes needed a quiet action to stay quiet. The kiln hall had enough notices already, and not every small mercy needed to become a public lesson before it could be trusted.

kiln_p17_053.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_053.text: At the next reserve check, Yue's compatible charge had improved through slower gathering, measured refinement loss and actual rest. The usable reading remained below the agreed thirty-six-unit threshold after the sampling discharge. She showed Luo the full page, including the cost of the improvement. He approved the continued bounded schedule rather than demand an immediate larger source allowance. Her posterior task still used the lower eighth input. The method was accumulating in weeks, not in a single dazzling night. She tucked the page into her private notes and went to help Zhu choose the least ridiculous tile for the exhibition.

kiln_p17_054.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_054.text: Before the display opened, Peng asked every maker what the public label would claim. Ordinary household bowl, observed drying comparison, accurately described art sample, failed guarded teaching cup: each had a different use. Zhu erased the word flawless from a draft while Tan groaned about losing attractive language. Yue wrote her own name only beside the cold display work she would actually perform. Jian checked the copied source dates. The table looked plain until Peng set the gray tile at one end and the deep-blue successor at the other. Visitors lingered between the gray tile and its blue successor.

kiln_p17_055.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_055.text: At the exhibition table, Yue placed the cracked drying sample beside the sound bowl and the notes. Visitors first reached for the prettier surface. She invited them to set each on the flat board and compare the feet without pretending touch could reveal every defect. One child declared the sound bowl boring. Zhu said boring bowls let soup be interesting. The child's grandfather bought two for that exact reason. The sale pleased the owner more than the possible prize. Tan recorded it, and Yue tucked the money receipt away from the teaching notes so nobody would mistake income for assessment.

kiln_p17_056.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_056.text: The rival pottery showed bright thin bowls under a polished sign. Yue recognized the workshop name from the earlier unsupported charged-ware offer, but the present ordinary bowls had their own use and records. She refused to transfer that old finding to every object on this table. Their clerk supplied the qualification notes when asked and grinned awkwardly at the mention of the past correction. 'We learned an expensive lesson,' he said. Yue bought nothing she could not carry in her habitual pack. She admired the glaze and returned to Zhu with a question about how thinness changed the drying risk.

kiln_p17_057.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_057.text: Zhu answered by letting her compare rejected rims, not by guessing at a competitor's hidden recipe. The exhibition judge joined them and asked about the archive display. He wanted a speech on cultivation changing craft. Luo gave him a cracked foot and said ordinary clay remained ordinary clay even beside an excellent cultivator. Yue described her actual sample work, including the guarded failed release cup at the home hall. The judge looked disappointed that nobody offered a spectacular claim, then spent longer at the small comparison than at the painted banner. The foot had given him something concrete to examine.

kiln_p17_058.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_058.text: Jian attended only the permitted cold exhibition duties with the assigned supervisor. A former learner recognized him from the public notice and asked if the live-vent story was true. He answered with the supported act and restriction. The man said apprentices had always been treated badly and laughed as though the hazard were a clever protest. Jian's face tightened. 'Han didn't agree to be the protest,' he said. The man lost his amusement. Yue heard the sentence while wrapping a sold bowl and felt something ease. The boy had refused a flattering account when accepting it would have been simpler.

kiln_p17_059.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_059.text: Later Jian admitted the refusal had felt awful. The stranger had been the first person to make him sound brave since the hearing. Zhu handed him a cloth and told him to polish the display board. 'You can feel awful while being right,' she said. He worked quietly, then asked if she had ever wanted an unfair compliment. She snorted. 'Have you seen my blue tile? I wanted six.' Yue laughed with them. The moment did not certify new trust, but it gave the day a lighter end than a solemn lesson would have managed.

kiln_p17_060.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_060.text: The hall did not win the main exhibition prize. It received a commendation for practical teaching, three modest household orders and a request for a later cold sample visit. The owner had wanted the prize bowl at the gate and looked disappointed for one honest minute. Then she checked the ordinary orders with Tan and declined the one whose delivery date exceeded the current schedule. 'I am improving,' she told Yue, 'but apparently not fast enough to enjoy it.' Yue said the donkey would approve a carrot budget. The owner threatened to put that wisdom in the next commercial notice.

kiln_p17_061.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_061.text: After the exhibition, the archive table had scuffs from handling and one missing comparison slip. Yue found the slip beneath the sold-bowl packing cloth before it left with a customer. She made a second checked copy and returned the original to Peng. The near loss had nothing dramatic about it, yet its prevention mattered as much as the public explanation. Zhu brought the gray first tile to join the display series. It looked less ridiculous beside its successor. The sequence had become a argument that a result could be beautiful, unreliable and useful to future work at the same time.

kiln_p17_062.speaker: narrator
kiln_p17_062.text: At the end of the twenty-eighth week, the water channel ran steadily and the covered tank held only its recorded remaining reserve. The summer still promised other interruptions. Yue's posterior eighth-input passage had repeated on recovered days with normal following checks, but she had not yet asked it to produce the useful quarter. Her anterior and arm tasks stayed at their known limits. The workshop smelled of new glaze, warm paper and ordinary wet clay. She sat beside Zhu's gray tile and the boy's corrected account, wondering which small thing the next month would teach her to see.
